lion.definition: A large wild cat; adult males usually have a mane.
lion.exampleUsage: The male lion rested with its mane visible.

elephant.definition: A very large mammal with a trunk and broad ears; tusk presence varies by species, sex and individual.
elephant.exampleUsage: The elephant lifted water with its trunk.

giraffe.definition: A tall African mammal with a very long neck and spotted coat.
giraffe.exampleUsage: The giraffe reached leaves high in the tree.

zebra.definition: Any of several fleet black-and-white striped African equines.
zebra.exampleUsage: The zebra's striped coat was visible from the viewing area.

hippopotamus.definition: Massive thick-skinned herbivorous animal living in or around rivers of tropical Africa.
hippopotamus.exampleUsage: The hippopotamus rested partly submerged in the water.

rhinoceros.definition: Massive powerful herbivorous odd-toed ungulate of southeast Asia and Africa having very thick skin and one or two horns on the snout.
rhinoceros.exampleUsage: The rhinoceros walked across the managed habitat.

cheetah.definition: Long-legged spotted cat of Africa and southwestern Asia having nonretractile claws.
cheetah.exampleUsage: The cheetah rested beneath the shade structure.

gorilla.definition: A very large African ape with dark fur and great strength.
gorilla.exampleUsage: The gorilla moved toward the sheltered area.

hyena.definition: A carnivorous mammal of the hyena family; feeding habits include hunting and scavenging depending on species.
hyena.exampleUsage: The hyena explored the enclosure ground.

wildebeest.definition: Large African antelope having a head with horns like an ox and a long tufted tail.
wildebeest.exampleUsage: The wildebeest grazed beside the other animals in its managed group.

gazelle.definition: Small swift graceful antelope of Africa and Asia having lustrous eyes.
gazelle.exampleUsage: The gazelle moved quickly across the open ground.

ostrich.definition: A very large African flightless bird with long legs and a long neck.
ostrich.exampleUsage: The ostrich ran on its long legs.

tiger.definition: A large wild cat with an orange coat and dark stripes.
tiger.exampleUsage: The tiger's striped coat was visible through the viewing window.

panda.definition: Large black-and-white herbivorous mammal of bamboo forests of China and Tibet.
panda.exampleUsage: The giant panda fed on bamboo.

orangutan.definition: Large long-armed ape of Borneo and Sumatra having arboreal habits.
orangutan.exampleUsage: The orangutan climbed using its long arms.

snow-leopard.definition: A large wild cat of the mountains of Central and South Asia, with thick pale fur and dark rosettes.
snow-leopard.exampleUsage: The snow leopard rested on a high rock.

red-panda.definition: A small reddish-brown mammal from the eastern Himalayas and southwestern China, with a long ringed tail.
red-panda.exampleUsage: The red panda climbed along a branch.

komodo-dragon.definition: The world's largest living lizard, native to several Indonesian islands.
komodo-dragon.exampleUsage: The Komodo dragon was observed from behind the barrier.

peacock.definition: The male of the peafowl, commonly known for its ornamental tail-covering feathers.
peacock.exampleUsage: The peacock spread its ornamental train.

water-buffalo.definition: A large domesticated bovine adapted to wet environments and widely used in parts of Asia for farming and dairy production.
water-buffalo.exampleUsage: The water buffalo stood near the pond.

cobra.definition: Venomous Asiatic and African elapid snakes that can expand the skin of the neck into a hood.
cobra.exampleUsage: The cobra raised its hood in the recorded observation.

macaque.definition: A monkey of the macaque group, with species native to Asia and North Africa and variable tail length.
macaque.exampleUsage: The macaque sat on a branch in its enclosure.

bald-eagle.definition: A large North American bird of prey with a white head and tail in adulthood.
bald-eagle.exampleUsage: The bald eagle perched above the river exhibit.

grizzly-bear.definition: An unusually large brown bear native to western North America.
grizzly-bear.exampleUsage: The grizzly bear searched the managed habitat.

bison.definition: Any of several large humped bovids having shaggy manes and large heads and short horns.
bison.exampleUsage: The bison grazed on the open ground.

wolf.definition: A wild canine that often lives and hunts in a group.
wolf.exampleUsage: The wolf moved with the other members of its group.

moose.definition: Large northern deer with enormous flattened antlers in the male.
moose.exampleUsage: The male moose's broad antlers were visible.

raccoon.definition: A mammal with a ringed tail and dark markings around its eyes.
raccoon.exampleUsage: The raccoon's ringed tail extended behind it.

skunk.definition: A mammal that can release a strong-smelling spray when threatened.
skunk.exampleUsage: The skunk walked toward its shelter.

otter.definition: A swimming mammal with thick fur and a long body that lives near water.
otter.exampleUsage: The otter swam through the water area.

beaver.definition: A large rodent with a flat tail that builds dams in waterways.
beaver.exampleUsage: The beaver carried a branch toward the bank.

cougar.definition: Large American feline resembling a lion.
cougar.exampleUsage: The cougar rested above the enclosure floor.

crocodile.definition: Large voracious aquatic reptile having a long snout with massive jaws and sharp teeth and a body covered with bony plates.
crocodile.exampleUsage: The crocodile lay beside the water.

alligator.definition: A large reptile with a broad snout, strong jaws, and a long tail.
alligator.exampleUsage: The alligator swam through the shallow pool.

iguana.definition: Large herbivorous tropical American arboreal lizards with a spiny crest along the back.
iguana.exampleUsage: The iguana rested on a branch.

chameleon.definition: A lizard of the chameleon family, with grasping feet and eyes that can move independently in many species.
chameleon.exampleUsage: The chameleon gripped the branch with its feet.

tortoise.definition: Usually herbivorous land turtles having clawed elephant-like limbs.
tortoise.exampleUsage: The tortoise walked across the dry floor.

python.definition: A large nonvenomous snake that kills prey by squeezing it.
python.exampleUsage: The python rested in coils beneath the shelter.

frog.definition: An amphibian commonly with strong hind legs in adulthood; habitat and diet vary by species.
frog.exampleUsage: The frog jumped from the bank.

salamander.definition: An amphibian usually with a long body and tail; life histories and water dependence vary by species.
salamander.exampleUsage: The salamander moved across the damp ground.

gecko.definition: A lizard of the gecko group; eye structures and activity patterns vary by species.
gecko.exampleUsage: The gecko rested on the enclosure wall.

rattlesnake.definition: Pit viper with horny segments at the end of the tail that rattle when shaken.
rattlesnake.exampleUsage: The rattlesnake shook its tail rattle.

parrot.definition: Usually brightly colored zygodactyl tropical birds with short hooked beaks and the ability to mimic sounds.
parrot.exampleUsage: The parrot gripped a branch with its feet.

flamingo.definition: Large pink to scarlet web-footed wading bird with down-bent bill.
flamingo.exampleUsage: The flamingo fed in shallow water.

toucan.definition: Brilliantly colored arboreal fruit-eating bird of tropical America having a very large thin-walled beak.
toucan.exampleUsage: The toucan's large bill was visible from the visitor path.

penguin.definition: A flightless bird with wings adapted for swimming, found mainly in the Southern Hemisphere.
penguin.exampleUsage: The penguin swam using its flipper-like wings.

owl.definition: A bird of prey with forward-facing eyes; many species are active mainly at night.
owl.exampleUsage: The owl turned its head toward the sound.

hawk.definition: A bird of prey commonly called hawk, with varied forms by species.
hawk.exampleUsage: The hawk watched the ground from its perch.

pelican.definition: A large waterbird with a long bill and expandable throat pouch.
pelican.exampleUsage: The pelican carried a fish in its bill pouch.

crane.definition: A tall long-legged bird with a long neck, often found near wetlands.
crane.exampleUsage: The crane walked through the wetland on its long legs.

hummingbird.definition: Tiny American bird having brilliant iridescent plumage and long slender bills.
hummingbird.exampleUsage: The hummingbird hovered beside a flower.

cockatoo.definition: A parrot of the cockatoo group, commonly with a movable crest; coloring varies by species.

enclosure.definition: A structure consisting of an area that has been enclosed for some purpose.
enclosure.exampleUsage: The enclosure separates the animal habitat from the visitor route.

cage.definition: An enclosure formed with bars or mesh for keeping animals.
cage.exampleUsage: The cage has mesh panels and a managed access door.

aquarium.definition: A tank or pool or bowl filled with water for keeping live fish and underwater animals.
aquarium.exampleUsage: The aquarium holds water for the displayed aquatic animals.

aviary.definition: A building where birds are kept.
aviary.exampleUsage: Birds flew within the large aviary.

gift-shop.definition: A shop selling souvenirs or items suitable as gifts.
gift-shop.exampleUsage: The gift shop sells souvenirs beside the exit.

ticket-booth.definition: A place where visitors buy or collect tickets.
ticket-booth.exampleUsage: The visitor collected a ticket at the ticket booth.

map.definition: A drawing that shows places, routes, and geographical features.
map.exampleUsage: The map shows the permitted visitor routes.

bench.definition: A long seat for several people.
bench.exampleUsage: The visitor rested on the bench beside the path.

fountain.definition: A structure that sends water upward and lets it fall back down.
fountain.exampleUsage: Water rose from the fountain and fell into its basin.

playground.definition: An area provided for play, often containing play equipment.
playground.exampleUsage: The playground contains equipment for play.

train-ride.definition: A ride in which passengers travel in a train around the park.
train-ride.exampleUsage: The train ride carries visitors around the grounds.

snack-bar.definition: A small business or counter that sells simple meals, snacks, and drinks for customers to eat there or take away.
snack-bar.exampleUsage: The visitor bought a sandwich at the snack bar.
